initial_prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: unapproved mobile home-page design-direction B decision comp for RC General Contracting Inc.
Create one high-fidelity flat mobile website screenshot at a 360 CSS-pixel logical width and about 900 CSS-pixel screenshot height, rendered sharply at 2x resolution (about 720 by 1800 pixels). It is one tall scrolling website view with no phone frame, no browser chrome, no perspective. Entire screenshot MUST be fully opaque, with flat pale board background #EFF3EC across all open space. Never make a transparent cutout.

Input images:
Image 1 is the existing RC logo; preserve the exact supplied full logo in a compact pure-white header container, without redrawing or replacing it.
Image 2 is the company's actual kitchen design rendering; preserve this supplied scene and drawing in the first full-width image.
Image 3 is the company's actual exposed framing construction photo; preserve this supplied photo as the next full-width image lower down.
Use only these image assets. They are not known to show the same project. The rendering must have caption "Design rendering"; the separate photo must have caption "During construction" when its lower edge is reached. No before/after implication, connecting arrows, project names or claims.

Mobile layout in exact top-to-bottom sequence:
1. Compact 72 CSS-pixel pale header, 24 CSS-pixel side gutters. At left a small approximately 48 CSS-pixel full existing logo in white. Beside it compact two-line brand text "RC General Contracting Inc". At right or on a compact second row, navigation "Services" and "Contact". Keep this practical and legible, not a large brand billboard. No hamburger needed.
2. Deep fir-green introductory block spans the full mobile content width, with 24 CSS-pixel internal side gutters. Start with eyebrow "Kincardine", then a bold sentence-case headline "General contracting, from plans to construction." in Archivo 600 at 40 CSS pixels and about 43 CSS-pixel line-height, pale ink. Aim for four short stacked lines: "General", "contracting,", "from plans to", "construction.".
3. Beneath the headline, readable 18 CSS-pixel Public Sans 400 body: "Residential and commercial renovations and new builds." Keep body at full content width, approximately two or three lines.
4. A rectangular lime #D8EC82 enquiry button with deep green ink, 48 CSS-pixel height and 18 CSS-pixel text, says exactly "Tell us about your project". Place it visibly below body inside the green block. Comfortable spacing, no oversized empty hero. Green block should finish around logical y=490 to y=530.
5. On the pale background below, 24 CSS-pixel gutters. First show the actual kitchen design rendering as a single large full-content-width 4:3 image (312 CSS pixels wide by 234 CSS pixels tall), starting around logical y=540, well before the first 800 CSS pixels. Caption "Design rendering" below, outside the image, in green at 15 CSS pixels.
6. After a clear vertical gap, start the actual construction photo as the next single full-content-width 4:3 image, equally 312 CSS pixels wide. It continues below the lower screenshot edge if necessary. Do NOT shrink it to squeeze it in. The two images are always vertically stacked, never thumbnails side by side. Its caption "During construction" follows the image in the continuing page.

Design system: flat pale board #EFF3EC, deep fir #173E33, pale body/heading ink, lime action #D8EC82 with fir ink, pale complementary #DCE6D7. Archivo 600 display plus Public Sans 400 body. Straight rectangular geometry, no shadows or rounded cards. An architectural board translated into a usable mobile home page. The green introduction and generous real imagery are the single dominant visual gesture.
Constraints: preserve exact brand name and copy; all type remains readable at a 360px screen width. Source logo and two images must remain recognizable. No invented photos, projects, stats, ratings, certifications, testimonials, added locations, phone or email. No diagrams, arrows, blueprint gridlines, tape, gradients, decorative lines, nested cards, or text laid over photos. Do not display breakpoint dimensions or design notes inside the UI. Solid fully opaque screenshot, never transparency.
